concepts.title: Stages in the Formation of a Company

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Stages in the Formation of a Company' refers to.
questions.a: The complete setup of a corporate enterprise encompasses distinct sequential phases starting from an initial venture concept to official registration and public fundraising.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Stages in the Formation of a Company'.
questions.a: Company formation progresses through promotion, incorporation, and capital subscription.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Stages in the Formation of a Company' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: 7.1 (source: kebs107.txt lines 30-55)

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Promoters and Their Primary Functions' refers to.
questions.a: A promoter is an individual or group that conceptualizes a business project, conducts feasibility analyses, and mobilizes key resources to bring the company into existence.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Promoters and Their Primary Functions'.
questions.a: Promoters identify opportunities, test feasibility, select names, and arrange necessary registration documents.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Promoters and Their Primary Functions' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: 7.2.1 (source: kebs107.txt lines 56-110)

concepts.title: Legal Position and Pre-Incorporation Liabilities of Promoters

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Legal Position and Pre-Incorporation Liabilities of Promoters' refers to.
questions.a: Promoters stand in a fiduciary relation to the company they create, barring them from making undisclosed profits while remaining personally liable for pre-incorporation agreements.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Legal Position and Pre-Incorporation Liabilities of Promoters'.
questions.a: Promoters owe fiduciary duties and carry personal liability for contracts executed before registration.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Legal Position and Pre-Incorporation Liabilities of Promoters' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: 7.2.1 (source: kebs107.txt lines 210-245)

concepts.title: Memorandum of Association and Its Essential Clauses

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Memorandum of Association and Its Essential Clauses' refers to.
questions.a: The fundamental charter of a corporate body that delineates its powers, scope of activities, capital structure, and external relationships.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Memorandum of Association and Its Essential Clauses'.
questions.a: MOA sets the boundaries and main objects beyond which a company cannot act.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Memorandum of Association and Its Essential Clauses' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: 7.2.1 (source: kebs107.txt lines 125-180)

questions.q: Calculate the remaining liability of a shareholder. Use the method 'Calculation of Unpaid Shareholder Liability'. Work with: face_value = 50000, paid_per_share = 50, shares_count = 4, unpaid_per_share = 100. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of the result.
questions.a: 400 rupees

questions.q: Find the unpaid share liability for a member. Use the method 'Calculation of Unpaid Shareholder Liability'. Work with: face_value = 2500, paid_per_share = 25, shares_count = 12, unpaid_per_share = 50. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of the result.
questions.a: 600 rupees

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Calculation of Unpaid Shareholder Liability' refers to.
questions.a: The maximum financial obligation of a shareholder in a company limited by shares, calculated as the unpaid balance on the nominal value of shares held.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Calculation of Unpaid Shareholder Liability'.
questions.a: A member's liability is strictly limited to the unpaid portion of their subscribed share capital.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Calculation of Unpaid Shareholder Liability', in plain ASCII form.
questions.a: total_liability = shares_count * (face_value - paid_per_share)

concepts.title: Articles of Association and Comparison with MOA

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Articles of Association and Comparison with MOA' refers to.
questions.a: A document containing internal governance rules that manage the operational management of a company, remaining subordinate to the Memorandum of Association.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Articles of Association and Comparison with MOA'.
questions.a: AOA governs internal administration while MOA defines external boundaries.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Articles of Association and Comparison with MOA' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: 7.2.1 (source: kebs107.txt lines 181-205)

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Statutory Documents for Company Registration' refers to.
questions.a: The requisite legal documentation including MOA, AOA, director consents, agreement, statutory declaration, and fee proof submitted to the Registrar.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Statutory Documents for Company Registration'.
questions.a: A company registration requires specific legal declarations, consents, and constitutional filings.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Statutory Documents for Company Registration' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: 7.2.1 (source: kebs107.txt lines 120-209)

concepts.title: Certificate of Incorporation and Legal Conclusiveness

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Certificate of Incorporation and Legal Conclusiveness' refers to.
questions.a: The official document issued by the Registrar of Companies certifying that a company is legally created, serving as irrefutable proof of legal personality.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Certificate of Incorporation and Legal Conclusiveness'.
questions.a: Certificate of Incorporation provides conclusive proof of the legal birth and existence of a corporate body.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Certificate of Incorporation and Legal Conclusiveness' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: 7.2.2 (source: kebs107.txt lines 246-300)

questions.q: Calculate the minimum subscription amount required. Use the method 'Calculation of Minimum Subscription'. Work with: total_issue_amount = 120000. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of the result.
questions.a: 108000 rupees

questions.q: Find the minimum subscription for an issue size. Use the method 'Calculation of Minimum Subscription'. Work with: total_issue_amount = 8000. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of the result.
questions.a: 7200 rupees

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Calculation of Minimum Subscription' refers to.
questions.a: The threshold minimum capital sum that must be subscribed by the public before a company can proceed with share allotment, mandated as 90 percent of the public issue.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Calculation of Minimum Subscription'.
questions.a: At least 90% of the public issue must be subscribed to validate allotment.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Calculation of Minimum Subscription', in plain ASCII form.
questions.a: min_subscription = total_issue_amount * 0.90

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Capital Subscription Formalities and Prospectus' refers to.
questions.a: The systematic procedure through which a public enterprise invites public capital contributions via prospectus filing, SEBI approval, stock exchange listing, and allotment.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Capital Subscription Formalities and Prospectus'.
questions.a: Public fundraising mandates SEBI clearance, prospectus registration, minimum subscription compliance, and return of allotment filing.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Capital Subscription Formalities and Prospectus' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: 7.2.3 (source: kebs107.txt lines 301-355)
